implementation_notes: The async Rust channel is tokio::sync::broadcast: Sender::subscribe creates a Receiver per subscriber, send clones the value to every receiver, and the capacity is a bounded ring buffer, so a receiver that falls behind receives RecvError::Lagged(n) instead of stalling the sender - the documented slow-receiver policy. Senders are cloneable (multi-producer) and dropping all of them closes the channel, which is the shutdown signal. Payloads are cloned per receiver, so send Arc<Event> for anything large. Without an async runtime, the standard-library registry is the alternative realization.
pitfalls: A lagging receiver loses messages silently unless RecvError::Lagged is handled; the error is the only notification of dropped events.
send() returns Err when there are no receivers at all, so a deliberately receiver-free publisher must ignore that result rather than unwrap it.
Cloning per receiver makes payload size multiply by subscriber count; send Arc<Event> instead of the full structure.

variants.name: std-only weak subscriber registry
variants.idiom_name: Mutex<Vec<Weak<dyn Fn(&Event) + Send + Sync>>> snapshotted on publish
variants.implementation_notes: With no async runtime the channel is an explicit registry of weak subscriber handles: subscribe stores a Weak (upgraded from an Arc the caller keeps), publish locks, snapshots the live strong references, releases the lock and then calls them, and dead Weak entries are pruned so the list does not grow forever. Dropping the owner silently unsubscribes, which removes the lifetime bug class at the cost of hand-written locking and no buffering or lag reporting. This is the realization to choose when the events are synchronous and the project must not take a runtime dependency.
pitfalls: Calling subscribers while holding the Mutex deadlocks as soon as a subscriber subscribes or unsubscribes.
Weak::upgrade returns None once the owner is dropped; prune dead slots or the registry grows silently.
A panic inside one subscriber poisons the Mutex for every later publish unless the lock is handled with catch_unwind or a poisoning-tolerant pattern.
